Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call today. Atlas is excited about Redwood for inference, but procurement asked me to put the ask in writing so we can align cross-functionally (finance + channel). Key constraints: a) we need a 20% effective discount at $2.2M ARR commit to match internal TCO targets, b) the reseller (CloudBroker) needs a protected margin of 12% on list in order to onboard and promote in their marketplace, and c) we need a fallback pricing band if usage spikes >1.5x in a quarter.

Can you confirm whether a conditional volume-coupling private offer is something you can support (i.e., list price anchor with a contingent credit and a protected reseller waterfall)? If so, please send a draft proposal and any required paperwork (procurement wants to see pass-through waterfall and a partner commission matrix).

Hi David — appreciate the clear summary. We can support a conditional private offer that pairs a list-price anchor with a triggered credit slab (the "coupling" you describe) and a reseller-protected waterfall. High level proposal: 

- Anchor list price at published marketplace SKU rates; apply an ARR-backed effective discounting schedule that yields ~20% effective at $2.2M commit.
- Reseller protection: 12% net margin guaranteed via a two-line waterfall: initial reseller commission (8% of list) + deal-level pass-through credit (4% of list) that ramps with usage tiers.
- Spike fallback: when monthly usage >1.5x forecasted, we apply a capped surge credit instead of re-pricing the whole contract (protects your renewals cadence).

I attached a short pricing-waterfall spreadsheet and a private-invoice (ATLAS_PI_v2.pdf) showing proposed numbers. Ben / Irene — can you review the margin mechanics and confirm we can commit to the 12% protection and the phrasing for the surge fallback? Procurement indicated they need the waterfall expressed as list-based pass-through rows for CloudBroker.

Next steps for Atlas: if you can sign the attached PI we will 1) create the private offer in Azure/GCP marketplace as requested and 2) route the partner commission to CloudBroker upon invoice settlement.

Best,

Sofia / Irene — quick internal note after scanning Sofia's draft. Overall signal is OK but two asks from legal/finance ops: 

1) Commission routing — CloudBroker wants an upfront carve (to pay promos) and a residual settlement on actual invoice. Finance prefers a single pass-through credit at month-end (less operational overhead). We can do either but we need to be explicit in the Marketplace PO that CloudBroker will receive "pass-through credit per invoice" and include a stub for promo payments.

2) 12% protected margin — we can guarantee equivalent economics to 12% but prefer framing as "reseller netback floor of 12% of list" with a reconciliation clause at quarter close (clears edge-case rounding/spikes).

3) Spike clause — recommend a capped surcharge credit (example: for spikes >1.5x, Atlas receives a 30% surcharge credit on incremental spend beyond the 1.5x threshold, capped at 6% of total bill for the quarter). That keeps you online while limiting our downside. Irene, can you confirm whether this surcharge-credit construct is deployable via the marketplaces' private-offer UI or if we must implement as a post-invoice credit?

If legal signs off we should be able to generate the PO and DocuSign by EOD.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Cloud GTM, Redwood Inference
